name: LabRAM Soleil

specs.Lasers: up to six motorized lasers (four built in, two external)
specs.Mapping: SmartSampling, up to 100x faster than a conventional Raman spectrometer (vendor claim, depends on configuration)

summary: Confocal Raman imaging microscope that HORIBA introduced at Pittcon 2020 as a multimodal UV-Vis-NIR system. It uses a sparse-sampling scheme (SmartSampling) to shorten hyperspectral Raman mapping.

sources.title: HORIBA Scientific announces LabRAM Soleil (Lab Manager)

name: DXR3xi Raman Imaging Microscope

resolution.note: vendor spatial resolution 0.5 µm, confocal depth 2 µm

summary: Benchtop confocal Raman imaging microscope with interchangeable pre-aligned lasers, filters and gratings and automatic alignment and calibration.

sources.title: DXR3xi Raman Imaging Microscope (Thermo Fisher catalog)

name: SENTERRA II
summary: Confocal Raman microscope built for automated, unattended operation with switchable built-in excitation lasers and continuous wavenumber calibration.

name: mIRage

resolution.note: set by the visible probe spot, independent of IR wavenumber (vendor)

specs.Method: optical photothermal infrared (O-PTIR): visible probe reads out pulsed mid-IR absorption
specs.Raman: mIRage-R measures IR and Raman at the same spot

summary: Infrared microscope that beats the IR diffraction limit by detecting the photothermal response to pulsed mid-IR light with a visible probe beam. The mIRage-R variant records Raman spectra from the same spot.
applications: Sub-micron IR spectroscopy of cells and polymers

name: SamuxMP

specs.Automation: SamuxMP Auto: up to 24 measurements in 90-180 min

summary: Mass photometer set up for adeno-associated virus (AAV) samples: it counts and weighs single capsids by interferometric scattering to give empty, partial and full capsid ratios.

name: CellVista SLIM

specs.Form: module that upgrades an existing microscope

summary: Commercial quantitative phase imaging module based on spatial light interference microscopy (SLIM), added to an existing phase contrast microscope to measure optical path length in unlabelled cells.
applications: Label-free cell growth and dry mass

sources.title: Phi Optics: CellVista SLIM, GLIM and AI
Wang et al. (2011) Spatial light interference microscopy (SLIM), Opt Express

name: LIFA
summary: Widefield frequency-domain FLIM system that attaches to the camera port of a microscope and records whole lifetime images at once instead of scanning.

name: iLas 2

resolution.note: axial resolution about 50 nm in TIRF theta-scan mode (vendor)

specs.Modes: azimuthal (ring) TIRF, 3D TIRF theta-scan, HILO, FRAP and photoactivation
specs.Versions: iLas 2 TIRF, FRAP (upright or inverted), TIRF/FRAP

summary: Laser illumination add-on that spins the TIRF beam around the objective back aperture (azimuthal TIRF) to even out interference fringes, and also steers the laser for HILO, FRAP and photoactivation.

sources.title: Ring TIRF system (UCSD Nikon Imaging Center)

name: MicAO 3DSR

specs.Position: between the microscope side port and the camera
specs.Hosts: inverted microscopes; plug-ins for µManager, MetaMorph, NIS-Elements

summary: Adaptive optics unit for single-molecule localization microscopy that corrects aberrations to restore a near-diffraction-limited, axially symmetric PSF. The vendor reports roughly twice the detected photons after correction.

name: Q2

specs.Detectors: GaAsP/GaAs PMTs, hybrid PMTs, SPADs; up to 5 channels
specs.Excitation: 375-1000 nm laser launcher, supercontinuum 400-950 nm, or fs lasers for 2-photon
specs.Methods: FLIM (frequency domain or TCSPC), FCS, FCCS, PCH, RICS, N&B, smFRET, antibunching

summary: Modular confocal system for time-resolved imaging and fluorescence fluctuation spectroscopy, combining FLIM, FCS-family methods and single-molecule FRET in one instrument.

sources.title: Q2 modular confocal microscope for FLIM and FFS (ISS)

name: Optical coherence tomography

specs.Principle: low-coherence interferometry, analogous to ultrasound pulse-echo
specs.Resolution: a few micrometres axially and laterally
specs.Sensitivity: reflections down to about 1e-10 of incident power

summary: First demonstration of OCT (Huang et al., Science 1991): cross-sectional images of scattering inside tissue from low-coherence interferometry, shown on retina and coronary artery in vitro.

sources.title: Huang et al. (1991) Optical coherence tomography, Science 254:1178

name: Optical coherence microscopy
summary: Combined coherence gating with confocal detection to improve optical sectioning deep in highly scattering media (Izatt et al., Optics Letters 1994).

sources.title: Izatt et al. (1994) Optical coherence microscopy in scattering media, Opt Lett 19:590

name: Functional photoacoustic microscope

specs.Depth: ratio of maximum imaging depth to depth resolution above 100

summary: Reflection-mode photoacoustic microscope that imaged optical absorption beyond the ~1 mm depth limit of optical methods, including haemoglobin oxygen saturation in single vessels (Zhang et al., Nature Biotechnology 2006).

sources.title: Zhang et al. (2006) Functional photoacoustic microscopy, Nat Biotechnol 24:848

name: Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscope (OR-PAM)
manufacturer: Wang lab (Washington University in St. Louis)
summary: Photoacoustic microscope with optically focused excitation that resolved single capillaries in living mice (Maslov et al., Optics Letters 2008).

sources.title: Maslov et al. (2008) Optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy for in vivo imaging of single capillaries, Opt Lett 33:929

name: Intrinsic emission multiphoton microscope
summary: Multicolour nonlinear microscopy of live tissue that combined two- and three-photon intrinsic fluorescence (NADH, retinol, indoleamines) with second harmonic generation from collagen to give histology-like images without stains (Zipfel et al., PNAS 2003).

sources.title: Zipfel et al. (2003) Live tissue intrinsic emission microscopy, PNAS 100:7075

name: Spatial light interference microscope (SLIM)

specs.Form: add-on module for an existing phase contrast microscope

summary: Quantitative phase method that combines Zernike phase contrast with holography-style phase retrieval to map optical path length in live cells; the paper reports topographic accuracy comparable to AFM at much higher speed (Wang et al., Optics Express 2011).

sources.title: Wang et al. (2011) Spatial light interference microscopy (SLIM), Opt Express 19:1016

name: Orientation-independent DIC
summary: DIC variant that computes phase-gradient and optical-path-difference images independent of the shear direction from images taken at several bias and shear orientations; special prisms switch orientation without rotating the specimen (Shribak and Inoue, Applied Optics 2006).

sources.title: Shribak, Inoue (2006) Orientation-independent differential interference contrast microscopy, Appl Opt 45:460

name: Light field microscope

specs.Principle: microlens array in the image plane of a conventional microscope
specs.Output: perspective views and focal stacks from one exposure; 3D deconvolution

summary: First light field microscope (Levoy et al., ACM Transactions on Graphics 2006): a microlens array captures spatial and angular information in a single snapshot, trading lateral resolution for refocusing and 3D reconstruction.

sources.title: Levoy et al. (2006) Light field microscopy, ACM Trans Graph 25:924

name: Fourier light-field microscope

specs.Principle: microlens array at the Fourier (pupil) plane
specs.Reported gains: two- to three-fold extended depth, about 100x faster reconstruction than conventional LFM

summary: Light-field design that records the light field in the Fourier domain, reducing reconstruction artefacts and computation compared with conventional light-field microscopy (Guo et al., Optics Express 2019).

sources.title: Guo et al. (2019) Fourier light-field microscopy, Opt Express 27:25573

name: High-NA oblique plane microscope
summary: Single-objective light-sheet microscope whose glass-tipped tertiary objective gives resolution comparable to lattice light-sheet square mode while keeping a standard sample mount (Sapoznik et al., eLife 2020).

sources.title: Sapoznik et al. (2020) A versatile oblique plane microscope, eLife 9:e57681

name: Epi-illumination SPIM
summary: Single-objective oblique light-sheet microscope with the sample interface of an ordinary inverted microscope, compatible with multi-well plates; it reached single-molecule sensitivity and imaged 16 cell lines in parallel (Yang et al., Nature Methods 2019).

sources.title: Yang et al. (2019) Epi-illumination SPIM, Nat Methods 16:501

name: 4Pi confocal fluorescence microscope

resolution.note: FWHM of depth discrimination, measured; NA 1.4 lenses, 633 nm excitation, ~725 nm detection

specs.Optics: Two opposing objectives illuminate and detect from both sides
specs.Axial resolution: About four times higher than a confocal fluorescence microscope

summary: Two opposing objective lenses focus onto the same point so that the excitation or detection wavefronts interfere, sharpening the focal spot along the optical axis. The measured depth discrimination was about four times finer than in a standard confocal microscope.

sources.title: Hell & Stelzer, J. Opt. Soc. Am. A 9:2159 (1992)

name: isoSTED
manufacturer: Hell lab (MPI for Biophysical Chemistry, Göttingen)

resolution.note: nearly spherical focal spots of 40-45 nm (lambda/16) diameter

summary: Combines STED with a 4Pi arrangement of two opposing lenses so that the effective focal spot shrinks along all three axes to a nearly spherical volume. Used to image the interior of cells, resolving sub-wavelength organelles.

name: RESOLFT with rsEGFP
manufacturer: Hell lab (MPI for Biophysical Chemistry, Göttingen)

resolution.note: <40 nm in living bacteria and mammalian cells

specs.Probe: rsEGFP, reversibly switchable more than a thousand times
specs.Light dose: Dendritic spines imaged with about a million times lower intensity than earlier nanoscopy

summary: RESOLFT nanoscopy of living cells and brain slices using rsEGFP, a reversibly photoswitchable green fluorescent protein. The same switching was used to write sub-diffraction features for data storage.

name: Total internal reflection fluorescence for cell-substrate contacts

specs.Excitation: Evanescent wave of a totally internally reflected laser beam
specs.Excitation depth: Within one light wavelength or less of the substrate

summary: First application of total internal reflection fluorescence to cultured cells, exciting only fluorophores at contacts between cells and the substrate. Demonstrated on rat myotubes with labelled acetylcholine receptors and on human fibroblasts with a lipid probe.

name: Highly inclined thin illumination (HILO)
summary: A highly inclined, thin beam illuminates a slab inside the cell, raising signal and lowering background compared with epi-illumination. This made single molecules visible deep inside mammalian cells and allowed 3D imaging.

name: Image scanning microscopy (ISM)

specs.Detection: Fast wide-field CCD records an image at each scan position

summary: A confocal laser scanning microscope in which the pinhole detector is replaced by a camera that records a small image at every scan point; combining these images doubles the lateral resolution. The paper set out the theory and first experimental realisation.

name: Multifocal SIM (MSIM)

specs.Pattern generator: Digital micromirror device (DMD) producing sparse multifocal patterns
specs.Depth: Zebrafish embryos imaged at depths >45 µm

summary: Sparse multifocal illumination from a DMD with pinhole-like rejection of out-of-focus light extended 3D SIM to samples about eightfold thicker than before. Built from commercial parts with open-source software.

name: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy
summary: First measurement of fluorescence fluctuations to obtain chemical rate constants and diffusion coefficients in a system at equilibrium. The test system was ethidium bromide binding to DNA.

sources.title: Magde, Elson & Webb, Phys. Rev. Lett. 29:705 (1972)

name: CARS microscope with near-infrared pulses
summary: A coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering microscope driven by near-infrared ultrashort pulses, giving label-free vibrational contrast with 3D sectioning in chemical and biological samples.

sources.title: Zumbusch, Holtom & Xie, Phys. Rev. Lett. 82:4142 (1999)

name: Stimulated Raman scattering microscope
summary: Three-dimensional label-free chemical imaging by stimulated Raman scattering, much more sensitive than spontaneous Raman microscopy, with background-free chemical contrast.

name: PAINT
summary: Points accumulation for imaging in nanoscale topography: fluorescent probes diffusing in solution bind the object, and each immobilised probe is localised at its centroid. The steady flux of probes allows very many localisations; shown on lipid bilayers and vesicles.

name: Structured-light optical sectioning

specs.Pattern: Single-spatial-frequency grid projected onto the sample
specs.Processing: Three images at different grid positions combined in real time

summary: A grid is projected into a conventional widefield microscope and three phase-shifted images are combined to give optically sectioned images similar to those of a confocal microscope.

name: Protein-retention expansion microscopy (proExM)
summary: A variant of expansion microscopy that anchors proteins themselves to the swellable gel, so standard fluorescent antibodies, streptavidin and fluorescent proteins can be used instead of custom reagents.
applications: Multicolour imaging of cells and mammalian tissue

name: In vivo two-photon imaging of neocortex
manufacturer: Svoboda, Denk, Kleinfeld & Tank (Murray Hill, New Jersey)
summary: Showed that two-photon laser scanning microscopy penetrates the scattering tissue of the intact brain, measuring stimulus-evoked dendritic calcium dynamics of layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons in rat barrel cortex in vivo.
